definition: A legal process by which the government seizes property — such as money, cars, or real estate — that it claims is connected to criminal activity, often without requiring a criminal conviction. Courts have held that civil forfeitures can qualify as 'fines' under the Eighth Amendment.
examples: Tyson Timbs, who filed an amicus brief in this case, had his Land Rover seized through civil forfeiture after a drug conviction, which led to the landmark 2019 Timbs v. Indiana ruling.
